A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bayesian-TPNN study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The theoretical Appendices I-K in v1 correspond to M-O in v2, allowing relocated material to be distinguished from additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original tabular prediction, synthetic component-selection and image classification results, together with appendix ablations, runtime comparisons and uncertainty analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds minibatch experiments, Deep Ensemble comparisons and a genomic classification study.

M1.justification: Appendix J adds a minibatch fitting variant, MBayesian-TPNN, representing a limited adaptation of data use during posterior fitting. The architecture, hierarchical priors and specified MH/Langevin moves remain unchanged; no modified minibatch acceptance rule is supplied. The expanded stepwise explanation describes an existing procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix L adds gene-expression classification on GSE43358: 57 samples, 54,675 features, and HER2-positive versus non-HER2-positive outcomes. This substantially extends coverage to a genomic domain with an extreme feature-to-sample ratio. Existing coverage is retained; the minibatch and Deep Ensemble studies reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: Appendix K/Table 29 adds Deep Ensemble as an evaluated comparator for prediction and uncertainty across all eight tabular datasets, substantially broadening the uncertainty comparison. Existing comparator sets remain. ANOVA-TPNN and NAM have dashes in genomic Table 30 because they could not be trained, so they are not evaluated genomic baselines.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include minibatch sizes of 1,000 for ABALONE and 2,000 for FICO, plus Deep Ensemble searches over ensemble sizes, architectures, learning rates, epochs and regularization. These accompany added experiments; the original 80/20 splits, evaluation metrics and reported training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix J/Table 28 adds a check of whether minibatching degrades prediction or uncertainty estimates. Appendix L/Table 31 adds a genomic component-ranking analysis, including a third-order interaction. The existing hyperparameter, proposal, stability, runtime, interpretation and distribution-shift analyses remain.

E5.justification: Five-trial averages and standard-error reporting remain the established practice, which the added experiments also follow. No new seed disclosure, significance-testing procedure or uncertainty-estimation method is introduced. Existing component credible intervals are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-27 retain their numerical results, while Tables 28-31 add minibatch scores, eight-dataset Deep Ensemble comparisons, and genomic prediction and component rankings. For example, genomic AUROCs are 0.949 (0.017) for Bayesian-TPNN, 0.545 (0.001) for Linear and 0.953 (0.041) for XGB. These substantially expand the reported findings.

T1.justification: v2 Appendices N.2-N.3 replace the scale domains (0, infinity) and (0, n] in v1 J.2-J.3 with [1/n, infinity) and [1/n, n]. This substantively restricts the theoretical function classes and sieves. The consistency conclusions and most derivations remain unchanged; Section 3.1 does not state a corresponding truncation of the Gamma prior.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient higher-order functional ANOVA estimation, improved prediction and uncertainty quantification, and posterior consistency. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly interprets minibatching as practically acceptable without meaningful performance degradation. Appendix L attributes the linear model's weak genomic performance to higher-order interactions and discusses computational infeasibility for ANOVA-TPNN and NAM. These extend the applicability and mechanism discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 documents minibatch sizes, the Deep Ensemble hyperparameter search grid, and the genomic dataset identifier and experimental setup. Existing preprocessing, hardware and supplementary-code statements remain unchanged. The minibatch likelihood and acceptance implementation are not explained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lakshminarayanan et al. (2017) for Deep Ensemble and Fumagalli et al. (2013) for GSE43358. Section 3.2 also makes the sampler's inspiration from BART more explicit. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized introduction edits and expanded explanations of architecture parameters and stepwise search. Four appendix sections are inserted before the relocated proofs, and acknowledgements and author information are updated. This is a limited structural and explanatory revision.

P2.justification: The ICLR format changes typography, text width, headers and figure/table placement throughout. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figures 7-9 add proposal illustrations, and Tables 28-31 display new experiments. Existing empirical plot images in Figures 2-6 are retained, with some relocated.

improvement.justification: The Deep Ensemble benchmark strengthens the uncertainty comparison, the genomic study tests substantially higher-dimensional applicability, and the proposal diagrams improve explanation. These provide a limited net gain. Minibatch implementation remains underspecified, the genomic explanation is not directly tested by an interaction ablation, and the proof's new 1/n scale restriction is not reconciled with the unchanged Gamma prior.
